The numeral type hierarchy: the probe's five traits, with no `comprises` clause; a program's type that extends one is refused by P-174's rule that a numeral type is written only as a parameter type.** The five: `Numeral extends Number`, `AnyNaturalNumeral` and `AnyRadixPointNumeral`, which exclude each other, and `NaturalNumeral[\nat n, nat r, nat v\]` and `RadixPointNumeral[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\]` below them, at the Draft's arities (PROBE `12. Decisions`, decision 1); the prelude's `Numeral` also excludes its number types. **Default: so, with a compiled test that `object O extends NaturalNumeral[\1, 10, 3\]` is refused.** Way not taken: `comprises` clauses, which can close only the three traits above the generic leaves, since the parser refuses an empty `comprises` (`parser/NoNewlineHeader.rats:104-108`, "Comprises clauses should not be empty."; PROBES, probe 4). The reason: P-176's one value per place, read where a place has one value for each instance.

# Rung T: the static numerals in the specification's revision form (rung-static-numerals-spec)

- problem: the specification states the field numerals, a numeral's four numbers as "fields of the numeral's value, not static parameters of its type" with the getters `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix` and `digitValue` (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:109-113` at b5b0f82c13; F-345), where P-174 and P-176 decide the static numerals (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:258-291`, rung T's section)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-148`, the Working Draft's numeral types and its coercions from numerals, the governing passage this rung revises; after the change `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-320`
- precedent: climb batch 29's rung T, which wrote the field numerals in the revision form and put its reasoning in its report, with no decision record (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-literals-spec/REPORT.md:1-8`); its entry `revival-numerals` rewritten in place under the same label, by fork T1 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:212`); the box form `\revision` (`Specification/fortress/fortress.tex:87`)
- deviation: no `decision-record.md` (`fortress-repo`'s `specification.md`, part 4): the section asks for none and the brief allows nothing else under `explorations/`; this report holds the full reasoning, and the entry cites it (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5210-5214`)
- deviation: the section title "A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie" and the entry's title "The numeral types, their conversion and their default" are kept, since ledger rows and tests cite them by title (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:302`; `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5010`)
- deviation: the normative text of `literals.tex` names the Java Virtual Machine's `int`, `long`, `float` and `double` (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:192-197`), as the section asks, beside the team's note that the chapter "specifies too much about the implementation" (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:321-324`)
- historical: `Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex`, `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex` (each present at `a874948ac`: `git cat-file -e a874948ac:<path>` succeeds for all nine)

Commits on `wip/rung-static-numerals-spec`: `4d2d895e8b` (the specification, 9 files, +475 −298) and `d3782350df` (`revival-numeral-type`'s power with a numeral exponent, 1 file). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` ("seeded from /home/user/fortress-base30 (dd00743d9e) in 3 s", exit 0) and its branch pushed.

## What changed and why

The decisions on record, the static numerals (P-174, P-176), with P-173's conversion, default and fold, P-40's bound for sizes, P-165's `asFloat`, P-37's exception for the prelude, and P-96's revision form, are written into the specification. The field numerals' sentences and boxes, climb batch 29's (`7daf51fe8a`), are replaced; Appendix I's `revival-numerals` is rewritten in place (fork T1), and no box names the field numerals. The Effects state the implementations as rung A leaves them (`CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:222-256` and forks A1 to A8, `:191-206`), with rows 957's second case and 971 written as open (forks A5, A6); the gather corrects them to what lands.

Passage by passage (lines after the change; "before" at b5b0f82c13):

1. **The numeral types** (`literals.tex:98-122`; before `:98-116`). Before: "Every numeral has the type \TYP{Numeral} ... through one of the two types that \TYP{Numeral} comprises ... \Library\ declare these numbers as the getters \VAR{digits}, \VAR{fractionDigits}, \VAR{radix} and \VAR{digitValue} ... They are fields of the numeral's value, not static parameters of its type: the three numeral types have no static parameters." After: "Every numeral has a \emph{numeral type} of its own, which exists only when the program is compiled: no value of a numeral type exists when the program runs. The static arguments of a numeral type are the numeral's \emph{four numbers}: ... Each of the four is a natural number, of any size. A numeral containing only digits has the type `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]`, and a numeral containing a radix point has the type `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]`. So `3.125` has the type `RadixPointNumeral[\4,3,10,3125\]`, `007` the type `NaturalNumeral[\3,10,7\]`, and `3000000000` the type `NaturalNumeral[\10,10,3000000000\]`." The hierarchy: `Numeral` extends `Number` with no static parameters; `NaturalNumeral` below `AnyNaturalNumeral`, `RadixPointNumeral` below `AnyRadixPointNumeral`, which exclude each other; none declares a method. Reason: P-174; PROBE `12. Decisions`, decision 1; fork A4 (`CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:202`); the team's two notes kept (`literals.tex:123-138`). Box: `revival-numerals` at `:146`.
2. **The radix** (`literals.tex:140-145`; before `:134-138`). Before: "such a numeral has the same type as one without an indicator. So `deadc_16` is a \TYP{NaturalNumeral} whose four numbers are $5$, $0$, $16$ and $912092$." After: "such a numeral has one of the same two numeral types, with its radix as the static argument $r$. So `deadc_16` has the type `NaturalNumeral[\5,16,912092\]`." Reason: P-174, the radix is `r`; PROBE `14. Where the Draft`.
3. **The box on the numeral types** (`literals.tex:146-161`, `revival-numerals`; before `:139-153`). Before: "The revival decided on 8~November 2026 that the four numbers are fields of the numeral's value: the two types with an explicit radix fold into the radix, and \TYP{Literal} into the digit count ... \TYP{Numeral} comprises the two numeral types." After: "The revival decided on 9~November 2026 that a numeral's type is the Working Draft's \TYP{NaturalNumeral} or \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}, at the Working Draft's arities, with the radix as the static argument $r$, and that it exists only when the program is compiled: the two types with an explicit radix are not built, since $r$ gives the radix, nor is \TYP{Literal}, and \TYP{Numeral} has no static parameters. So the team's draft notes above are answered: no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, and this section gives the hierarchy of the numeral types." Fork T1.
4. **The conversion** (`literals.tex:165-197`; before `:155-175`). The Draft's sentences kept as batch 29 kept them (`:165-180`). Before: "each of the eight number types ... declares a coercion from \TYP{NaturalNumeral}, and ... one from \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}; the conversion is exact ...". After: the same coercions, "each generic over the four numbers, as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} declares `coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\])`. The parameter of such a coercion has no value: its body computes the type's value from the four numbers, which it reads as values, integers of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\secref{natparams}). ... At a numeral, the compiler instantiates the coercion at the numeral's four numbers and evaluates it: a value that the Java Virtual Machine holds as an `int`, a `long`, a `float` or a `double` is a constant of the compiled code, and any other value, as one of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} or \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, is made once for the place where the numeral stands". Reason: P-174, P-176, P-40; the section's bullet; the declarations of the patch (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-30/probes/draft-numerals.patch:1-207`, `:760-858`).
5. **A place that fixes a type** (`literals.tex:199-201`; before `:177-180`). Before: "... as each number type of \library\ does and a type of a program's own may, or is a numeral type itself." After: the last clause removed. Reason: P-174's written-only rule; PROBE `1. Where the snapshot`; the patch refuses a binding at a numeral type (`tests/NumeralTypeNoValueWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/LiteralTypeUnwritable.fss`). P-173's "is a numeral type" is not written (reserved point).
6. **A type of a program's own** (`literals.tex:229-267`; before `:207-229`). Before: "receives a numeral through its own coercion from the numeral's type, such as `coerce(x: RadixPointNumeral)`, whose body reads the four numbers ... a negative constant reaches it as the prefix operator \EXP{-} ... Inside the body of a coercion, two values of a numeral type are equal, and strictly equivalent, when their values $v/r^m$ are equal". After: the coercion generic over the four numbers, with the Working Draft's interval as a Fortress block (`:235-241`, P-174's example: `coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Interval(roundDown(v, r, m), roundUp(v, r, m))`); no coercion, no chain, a static error; "The coercion receives the four numbers of a numeral as written. A numeral as written under the prefix operator \EXP{-}, as \EXP{-3}, is that operator of the type applied to the coercion's result for the numeral, so a type without that operator refuses it; any other static expression of numerals alone is folded first ... and reaches the type only through the type's coercion from the folded constant's default type, as \EXP{1/2} through a coercion from \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}"; a `where` clause that compares the four numbers, a static error, as `300` at a byte type with `where {v < 256}`; once per place "with the type's prefix \EXP{-} where the numeral is negated"; written only as a parameter type, "nor as a type that a trait or an object extends". The sentence on two numeral values inside a coercion's body is removed. Reason: P-174 (sign, chain, written-only), P-176, fork A4, fork T3, SNAP `3. The design` point 8 (the byte type) and `11. Consequences`.
7. **The box after it** (`literals.tex:268-285`, `revival-numerals`; before `:230-245`). Before: "The revival decided on 8~November 2026 that ... a type of a program's own receives a numeral only through its coercion from the numeral's type, once for each place; and that the numeral types are written only as parameter types." After: 8 November for the conversion where it stands, the written-only rule and the minus; "It decided on 9~November 2026 that every number type, of \library\ and of a program, receives a numeral through a coercion generic over the four numbers, which the compiler instantiates at the numeral and folds, and that a numeral at a place denotes one value, made once, the same on both implementations. The interpreter, which has no static types, applies the coercion at the place's first evaluation and refuses a numeral only there"; `IntLiteral` "the name that the compiled path's own library gave it".
8. **The box on static rational expressions** (`literals.tex:313-320`; before `:268-273`). Gains: "since at a number type of \library\ it is converted from its exact value; a type of a program's own receives it through its coercion from the constant's default type." Fork T3.
9. **The types chapter** (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:576-588`; before `:576-583`). Before: "\TYP{Numeral}, whose values carry a numeral's four numbers ... as fields", box "the revival decided on 8~November 2026 that they are fields of the numeral's value". After: "the numeral types below \TYP{Numeral}, `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]` and `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, which exist only when a program is compiled, for appropriate values of \VAR{b}, \VAR{n}, \VAR{m}, \VAR{r}, and \VAR{v}"; box: 9 November, the static arguments, no value when a program runs.
10. **The numbers chapter** (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:47-56`, `:58-71`, box `:64`; before `:47-55`, `:56-69`). Before: "Each type that coerces from a numeral type declares \EXP{=} with it, ... so that \EXP{u = 0} is \VAR{true} for a zero \VAR{u} of any of the eight types"; "The two numeral types declare \VAR{asFloat} too". After: each coercion generic over the four numbers, "Since no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, a numeral type declares no \EXP{=} with a number type, and no number type declares one with a numeral type"; "\TYP{Number} itself declares no conversion, and the numeral types declare no \VAR{asFloat}"; box: 9 November, generic coercions, no `asFloat`, no `=`. Reason: P-165, SNAP `11. Consequences` ("It was a wrong choice and it gets deleted").
11. **The coercion chapter** (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:84-87`, `:91-92` inside `revival-int-float`; box `revival-numerals` `:121-129`). Before: "\Library\ give an integer numeral the type \TYP{NaturalNumeral}, from which \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} coerces with one rounding"; "declares no coercion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} from an integer type or an integer numeral". After: "a type `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]`, from which \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} coerces by a coercion generic over the numeral's four numbers, with one rounding"; "from an integer type or from \TYP{NaturalNumeral}". Box gains: "It decided on 9~November 2026 that a numeral's coercion into a type is the one that the type declares from the numeral's type, generic over the numeral's four numbers ..., for the number types of \library\ as for a type of a program's own."
12. **The inference chapter** (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:305-308`, box `:346-355`). Before: "A numeral has a type of its own, from which \library\ define coercions to the number types". After: "A numeral has a numeral type of its own, whose static arguments are the numeral's four numbers, and from which \library\ define coercions to the number types, generic over those numbers"; the box gains the 9 November sentence. The box at `:188` stands (it names no numeral type's form).
13. **The `nat` parameters** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:105-121`, box). Gains: "The revival decided on 9~November 2026 that the four numbers of a numeral type (\secref{literals}) are \KWD{nat} parameters of any size, which, read as values in the body of a coercion from that type, are integers of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}: the bound of a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter to the range of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, which the compiled type checker enforces, is this implementation's bound for sizes, such as the length of an array, and not a bound of these four numbers." Reason: P-40, P-174.
14. **The constant chapter** (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:92-104`, boxes `:113-126`, `:144-148`). Before: "where a place fixes a type, the constant is converted into it as a numeral is, with at most one rounding." After: "Where a place fixes a number type of \library, the constant is converted into it from its exact value, exactly or with one rounding, and a constant outside the type's range is a static error. Only a numeral as written reaches a coercion from a numeral type (\secref{literals}): at a type of a program's own, a negated numeral as written is the type's prefix operator \EXP{-} applied to the coercion's result for the numeral, and any other signed constant reaches the type only through the type's coercion from the constant's default type, as \EXP{1/2} through a coercion from \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}." Box `:113` gains the 9 November sentence; box `:144`: "so that the four numbers of its type (\secref{literals}) count them". Fork T3, fork A3.
15. **The binary chapter** (`Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex:925`, `:1146`, `:1752`, `:1779`, `:1905`, `:2141`, `:2168`, `:2344`; before `:925`, `:1146`, `:1752`, `:1781`, `:1907`, `:2143`, `:2172`, `:2348`). Before: "The revival's numeral types have no static parameters: the four numbers of a numeral are fields of its value (\secref{literals}), and a field cannot give a static size, so no library can declare these operators as written". After (operators): "take the numeral's digit count, radix and value as static parameters, as the revival's numeral type `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]` has them (\secref{literals}), so a library could declare them as written. The revival leaves them out (\secref{revival-numerals}), and no library declares them. The declarations stand as the Working Draft gives them."; the coercion boxes add "their \KWD{where} clauses taking a static size from the digit count and the radix". Fork T2; P-174, "The design leaves out the binary chapter's numeral coercion and `opr ||`"; SNAP `2. The Working`, "which he declined to fulfil at 23:02".
16. **`comprehensions.tex` and `concrete-syntax.tex`**: unchanged. They name no numeral type, only the grammar's nonterminal `IntLiteralExpr` (`Specification/basic/expressions/comprehensions.tex:42`, `Specification/appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex:534`, `:1099`), which the Working Draft has at the same lines.

## Appendix I: `revival-numerals` as written

`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5010-5486`, rewritten in place under its label (fork T1); no sentence of it names the field numerals.

- **Affected sections** (`:5014-5020`): as before, plus `\secref{revival-native-helpers}`.
- **Change** (`:5021-5102`): `literals` gives every numeral a numeral type of its own, existing only when the program is compiled, `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]` or `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, the four numbers its static arguments, each a natural of any size; `Numeral` without static parameters through two traits that exclude each other; no explicit-radix types and no `Literal`. `types-libraries`; the conversion; the coercions generic over the four numbers, read as `ZZ`, folded to a JVM constant or made once per place; a place fixes a type where its type declares a coercion from the numeral's type; the default; a program's type through its own coercion, the interval as the example; the numeral as written, the minus, other static expressions through the default's type; the `where` clause; once per place, the minus with it; written only as a parameter type, never in an `extends` clause. `static-expr`, `coercion`, `static-arg-inference`, `numeral-default`, `basic-rationals`, `natparams`, the binary chapter's eight boxes; the five entries revised "where they named \TYP{IntLiteral}, a numeral's value, the numeral types' \VAR{asFloat}, the pairs of \EXP{=} with a numeral type or a power with a numeral exponent, or said what the interpreter does with a numeral".
- **Rationale** (`:5103-5215`): 8 November 2026 (converted where it stands, the default, the fold, the minus at a program's type, the written-only rule); 9 November 2026 (the Working Draft's types with the four numbers as static arguments, compile time only; every number type through a coercion generic over them, instantiated and folded; one value per place, a constant or a value made when the class loads, or under walk at the first evaluation); the Draft's ground (`literals.tex:132-148`, `:83-129`); the team's commit `128f313b5b` (`git log -1 --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short 128f313b5b`: "128f313b5b 2009-11-17 [libraries, codegen] ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as described in the spec. ..."); the 16-bit floating-point type rounding once; the library's types through the same coercion; the explicit-radix types and `Literal` not built, `Numeral` without static parameters by the probe's decision 1 (cited); the two `Any` traits as `AnyIntegral` serves the integers (PROBE `3. Step 2`); no numeral value, so no method, `asFloat` or `=`, the team's "IntLiterals should always be transient objects with minimal lifetime" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java:21-23`, cited at b5b0f82c13, since fork A8 may delete the file) carried to its end; no sign; the fold; the binary chapter now expressible and declined on 8 November 2026; the default, the exact defaults declined (`literals.tick:25`); P-26's bend in two places, now "names, its static parameters and the default"; the `nat` value `ZZ32` and the four numbers `ZZ`; no chain; the reversals (the Draft's polymorphic numerals; the team's run-time `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral`); the full reasoning (the snapshot, the probe report, the judgement of 8 November, this report).
- **Effect** (`:5216-5311`): batch 29's repairs (rows 943, 944, 454, 946, 79, 325, 862, 486), `round(2.50000000000000001)`, printing at the default (the clause on printing a value of a numeral type removed); no numeral value on either implementation; the prelude's numeral types and coercions, no `QQ`; the compiled fold of a numeral as written through the type's coercion, the one method of the four numbers as `ZZ` called once per place in the class's initialization, the minus with it (forks A1, A2, A's step 4); a signed constant at a library type converted from its exact value on both paths (fork A3); walk at the first evaluation, its refusals when the place runs; row 967; rows 395, 511; the checker's exemption of the libraries; `u = 0` under walk `false`, `u ≠ 0` `true` (rows 966 and NEW-A-1, `tests/XXXNumeralEqualsNumberWalk.fss`), open; compiled `u = 0` `true`; the departures 958, 960, 963, 957 (second case, open), 971 (open), 962, 956; the model program.
- **Original text** (`:5312-5481`): the Working Draft's quotes kept; the binary quote's lead-in "which the change contradicts" becomes "which the change leaves out".
- **Route C** (`:5482-5485`): "The same under route~C: the numeral types lie below \TYP{Numeral}, beside the number types under \TYP{Number}, and no number type is a subtype of a numeral type or a numeral type of a number type, whichever rule on instantiations the compiled type checker keeps."

## Each other entry revised, before and after

- `revival-asfloat` (`changes.tex:2757`). Rationale before: "\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and the two numeral types \TYP{NaturalNumeral} and \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}"; after (`:2780-2787`): "\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} ... The revival decided on 9~November 2026 that the numeral types declare none, since no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs". Effect before: "for each of the library's fourteen coercions between number types, and each of its eleven from the two numeral types (\secref{revival-numerals}), the type converted to declares \EXP{=} ..."; after (`:2794-2800`): the fourteen keep their pairs; "The library's eleven coercions from the two numeral types have no such pairs". The fourteen are unchanged by the patch (it changes no coercion between number types: `draft-numerals.patch:1-207`, `:760-858`).
- `revival-numeral-type` (`changes.tex:3753`). Change before: "an integer numeral has the type \TYP{NaturalNumeral}, beside \TYP{RadixPointNumeral} ... of 8~November 2026"; after (`:3764-3771`): "of 8 and 9~November 2026 ... `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]`, beside `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]` ..., types that exist only when a program is compiled and whose static arguments are the numeral's four numbers". Effect before: "named \TYP{NaturalNumeral} in \library\ ...; the compiled path's own library keeps the name \TYP{IntLiteral}"; after (`:3794-3797`): replaced in both libraries by `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]`, "of which no value exists when a program runs". Before: "\library\ state on each integer type the comparisons ..., \OPR{MAXNUM}, \OPR{MINNUM} and a power with a numeral exponent"; after (`:3805-3812`): without the power, and "They stated a power with a numeral exponent too, which the change of \secref{revival-numerals} removes: a numeral exponent reaches the power's declarations over \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \TYP{AnyIntegral}" (the patch deletes `opr ^(self, b:NaturalNumeral)` on the five integer types: `draft-numerals.patch:1-207`, `:760-858`). Before: "Equality is stated in pairs instead ..."; after (`:3813-3824`): "Equality was stated in pairs ...; since the change of \secref{revival-numerals} no such pair exists"; inequality: "so on the interpreter \EXP{u \neq 0} is \VAR{true} ..., and \EXP{u = 0} is \VAR{false}, as the effect of \secref{revival-numerals} says with its rows". "\TYP{NaturalNumeral} declares none of them, nor any other method".
- `revival-inference` (`changes.tex:1935`). Rationale gains (`:2243-2246`): "The four numbers of a numeral type, read as values in the body of a coercion from it, are integers of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} instead, since the revival decided on 9~November 2026 that they are naturals of any size". Its Change (`:1960-1966`) and Effect (`:2263-2266`) stand: they speak of the default.
- `revival-object-kinds` (`changes.tex:4046`). Effect before: "\Library\ declare the rational type's object and the two numeral types, \TYP{NaturalNumeral} and \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}, as value objects."; after (`:4084-4086`): "\Library\ declare the rational type's object as a value object; the numeral types are traits of which no value exists when a program runs".
- `revival-native-helpers` (`changes.tex:4631`), not on the section's list, named by the manifest's blurb ("the entries that name a numeral type's getters, asFloat, pairs or IntLiteral revised"). Effect before: "into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} for the numeral types' \VAR{asFloat} and the coercions of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}"; after (`:4694-4696`): "into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} for the coercions of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}". The count "374 of the 402 bindings" stands: the patch removes no `builtinPrimitive` binding (no line that its library hunks add or remove holds one: `sed -n 208,421p draft-numerals.patch | grep -c '^[-+].*builtinPrimitive'` and the same over `809,857p`, the hunks of `FortressLibrary.fss` and `FortressBuiltin.fss`, each print 0), and `numeralRR64` and `numeralRR32` stay (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:669`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:209`).

**The change.**
- The team's source: the Working Draft gives a numeral six types, `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]` (and `Literal[\v\]` without leading zeros), `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[\n,r,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeralWithExplicitRadix[\n,m,r,v\]` and `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]` above all (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-129`), says that "Numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types" (`:132-141`) and that libraries define coercions from numerals (`:146-148`), and says nothing of a numeral's value when a program runs or of when a coercion is applied. The team's compiled library types numerals by run-time values, `trait IntLiteral` and `trait FloatLiteral` with getters such as `asZZ32` and `asRR64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:390`, `:479`, at b5b0f82c13), whose coercions run on that value.
- What the text now says: a numeral's type exists only at compile time, `NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]` or `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]`, at the Draft's arities with the radix as `r`, below a `Numeral` without static parameters; the explicit-radix types and `Literal` are not built; no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, so a numeral type has no method, no `asFloat` and no `=` with a number type; every number type, the library's and a program's, takes a numeral through `coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\])` or its radix-point form, whose body reads the four numbers as `ZZ` values; the compiler folds it to a constant, or makes the value once per place; `-3` at a program's type is the type's own `-` on the coercion's result for `3`; a `where` clause over the four numbers refuses a numeral statically (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-285`; `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5010-5486`). The tests that show the tree doing so land with the code: `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralStaticDesignWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralOwnTypeWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralTypeNoValueWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NumeralStaticDesignCompiled.fss` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNumeralWhereRefusedCompiled.test`.
- The reason, as evidence: the Draft's own ground, "This approach allows library designers to decide how numerals should interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:142-145`), which a coercion that sees only a value cannot carry out: a 16-bit float type's coercion from the four numbers rounds `1.00390625000000000001` once, to `0x3F81`, where a coercion from an `RR64` gives `0x3F80` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NumeralStaticDesignCompiled.fss`, "BF16(1.00390625000000000001) rounds once, to 0x3F81"); a JVM class file holds no object constant, so a value at a place is a constant or a field filled once when the class loads; the team's own word on the run-time value, "IntLiterals should always be transient objects with minimal lifetime" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java:21-23` at b5b0f82c13).

**Provenance.** The curator's design of the static numerals, confirmed on 9 November 2026 (P-174, P-176), with P-173's conversion, default and fold, P-40's bound for sizes, P-165's `asFloat` and P-37's exception for the prelude; the specification written in the revision form (P-96) by climb batch 29b's rung T, with the forks T1 (the entry rewritten in place), T2 (the binary chapter) and T3 (the constant chapter) at their defaults, and the Effects from the forks A1 to A8 of the same batch.

\subsection{The numeral types, their conversion and their default}
\seclabel{revival-numerals}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{literals}; \secref{types-libraries}; \secref{static-expr};
\secref{coercion}; \secref{static-arg-inference}; \secref{numeral-default};
\secref{basic-rationals}; \secref{natparams}; \secref{lib:BinaryEndianWord};
\secref{lib:BinaryLinearEndianSequence};
\secref{lib:BinaryEndianLinearEndianSequence}; \secref{revival-numeral-type};
\secref{revival-inference}; \secref{revival-asfloat};
\secref{revival-object-kinds}; \secref{revival-native-helpers}.
\item[Change] \secref{literals} says that every numeral has a numeral type of
its own, which exists only when the program is compiled, so that no value of a
numeral type exists when the program runs: the Working Draft's
\EXP{\TYP{NaturalNumeral}\llbracket{}n,r,v\rrbracket} for a numeral without a
radix point, and \EXP{\TYP{RadixPointNumeral}\llbracket{}n,m,r,v\rrbracket} for
one with a radix point, whose static arguments are the numeral's four numbers,
its digit count $n$, the number $m$ of its digits after the radix point, its
radix $r$ and the value $v$ of its digits, each a natural number of any size;
that \library\ declare the two types below a \TYP{Numeral} without static
parameters, which extends \TYP{Number}, through two traits that exclude each
other, none of them with a method; and that the radix is the static argument
$r$, so that the two types with an explicit radix are not built, nor is
\TYP{Literal}.
\secref{types-libraries} names the two numeral types below \TYP{Numeral} among
the standard types for literals, as types that exist only when a program is
compiled.
Its paragraph that said that numerals are not directly converted now says that a
numeral is converted where it stands, and its sentences on library designers
and their coercions stand.
New paragraphs say that each number type of \library\ declares its coercion from
a numeral type generic over the four numbers, whose parameter has no value and
whose body computes the type's value from the four numbers, read as values of
type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}: exactly into the integer types and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, and
with one rounding into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}; that the
compiler instantiates the coercion at the numeral and evaluates it, so that a
value that the Java Virtual Machine holds as an \texttt{int}, a \texttt{long}, a
\texttt{float} or a \texttt{double} is a constant, and any other value is made
once for the place; that a place fixes a type where the type declared there
declares a coercion from the numeral's type, and that a numeral outside that
type's range is a static error; that elsewhere a numeral is converted into its
default, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} by its value,
or \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} with a radix point, the default applying to a numeral and
never to an expression of a numeral type; that a type of a program's own
receives a numeral only through its own coercion generic over the four numbers,
the Working Draft's interval being the example; that the coercion receives a
numeral as written, a negated numeral being the type's prefix \EXP{-} on the
coercion's result for the numeral, and any other static expression of numerals
reaching the type only through its coercion from the folded constant's default
type; that a \KWD{where} clause of the coercion that compares the four numbers
refuses a numeral statically; that the coercion is applied once for each place,
the prefix \EXP{-} with it, so that the place denotes one object; and that a
numeral type is written only as a parameter type, never as a type that a trait
or an object extends.
Its box on the numeral's type is rewritten, and so are its boxes after the
paragraph on a type of a program's own and after the paragraph on static
rational expressions.
\secref{static-expr} says, after its list of the traits of static expressions,
that \library\ declare no constant trait and that an expression of numerals and
operators is folded exactly into a signed constant, which takes one of three
defaults where nothing fixes its type, is converted from its exact value at a
number type of \library, and reaches a type of a program's own as a negated
numeral as written or through the type's coercion from its default type, and
which operators the fold leaves alone; a box follows, and another follows the
paragraph on the concatenation of literals, which says that the concatenation of
two natural numerals is built.
\secref{coercion} says that a numeral's conversion into its default is a rule
beside coercion, that a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of
its default type and to one that fixes no type, and that a type of a program's
own without a coercion from the numeral's type refuses a numeral, with a box;
its box on integers in floating-point expressions names the type
\EXP{\TYP{NaturalNumeral}\llbracket{}n,r,v\rrbracket} and the coercion generic
over the four numbers, and no longer says that the interpreter leaves a large
numeral unconverted.
\secref{static-arg-inference} says that \EXP{\VAR{id}(3)} is instantiated at the
numeral's default, with a box.
\secref{numeral-default} gives the numeral's own type with its four numbers as
static arguments, the default at every place that fixes no type, the narrowest
default for a type parameter or the branches that several numerals fix, and the

content.content:
It decided on 9~November 2026 that a numeral's type is the Working Draft's
\TYP{NaturalNumeral} or \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}, below \TYP{Numeral}, with the
four numbers as its static arguments, naturals of any size, and that it exists
only when the program is compiled; that every number type, of \library\ and of a
program, receives a numeral through a coercion generic over the four numbers,
which the compiler instantiates for the numeral and folds; and that a numeral at
a place denotes one value, the same on both implementations, made once: a
constant where the Java Virtual Machine holds the value as an \texttt{int}, a
\texttt{long}, a \texttt{float} or a \texttt{double}, and otherwise a value made
when the class that holds the place is loaded, since a class file holds no
object, or, in the interpreter, at the place's first evaluation.
The Working Draft gives numerals types of their own so that library designers
decide by coercions how numerals meet other types, and so that an interval type
receives \EXP{3.1415926535897932384} unrounded
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
132--148); it gives the numeral types the four numbers as static arguments
(lines 83--129), and says nothing of a value of a numeral type or of when a
coercion from one is applied.
The team built a coercion from a numeral type under its own names, in the
compiled path's own library (``ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as described in the
spec'', the team's commit \texttt{128f313b5b} of 17~November 2009, in the
revival's repository), applied at run time to a numeral value that carries its
exact value but not the four numbers.
The change finishes the Working Draft's design: a coercion from a numeral type
is the interface through which a number type receives the four numbers that the
parser reads, and its body calls the type's constructor on values computed from
them, so that a 16-bit floating-point type of a program's own rounds
\EXP{1.00390625000000000001} once, to the 16-bit value nearest to the numeral,
where a coercion that received a floating-point value would round it first to
the nearest \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and then to another 16-bit value.
The number types of \library\ receive a numeral through the same coercion as a
type of a program's own, as the Working Draft has libraries define the coercions
from numerals into integers and rationals.
The Working Draft's two types with an explicit radix are not built, since $r$
holds the radix, nor is its \TYP{Literal}; and \TYP{Numeral}, above both numeral
types, takes no static parameters, which, as the revival's prototype of the
design found, the rule that no type extends two instantiations of one generic
trait forbids beside the two generic numeral types
(\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/plan-30/probes/draft-numerals.md},
section~12, in the revival's repository).
\TYP{AnyNaturalNumeral} and \TYP{AnyRadixPointNumeral} exclude each other so
that a type's two coercions from the numeral types are valid overloads, as
\TYP{AnyIntegral} above \TYP{Integral} serves the integer types of \library.
No value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, so a numeral type declares
no method, no \VAR{asFloat} and no \EXP{=} with a number type; the team's one
word on a numeral's value at run time, that ``IntLiterals should always be
transient objects with minimal lifetime''
(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java},
lines 21--23, in the revival's repository at commit \texttt{b5b0f82c13}), is
carried to its end.
A numeral has no sign: at a type of a program's own a negated numeral is the
type's own prefix \EXP{-} applied to the coercion's result, and a type without
that operator refuses it, while at a number type of \library\ the folded
constant is converted from its exact value, so that \EXP{-2147483648} is a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}.
An expression of numerals alone is folded exactly, as the Working Draft computes
a static rational expression exactly and rounds it at most once
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
162--173); its result is a signed constant written as numerals, not a value of a
constant trait, so that a coercion from a numeral type receives only the four
numbers of a numeral as written, any other constant reaching a type of a
program's own only through that type's coercion from the constant's default
type, since coercion does not chain, and \EXP{x = 7/2} stays a rational.
With the four numbers as static parameters, the binary chapter's static word
width from a numeral's digit count and radix can be declared; the revival
declined on 8~November 2026 to build it, its coercions from a numeral type being
those of the number types and of a program's own types, and the binary chapter's
coercion and its \EXP{\|} with a numeral stand, each with a box.
The default is the type that the interpreter already gave an integer numeral by
its value, and the Java programming language's type for an integer literal.
The revival declined exact defaults, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, as
the team's restart of 2012 gives \EXP{\mathbb{N}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}
(\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick},
line 25), since its model program's constants declared without a type would then
be rationals and every index declared without a type would need a conversion.
In two places the change departs from the revival's rule that the team's later
decision wins over its earlier one: the compiled path's own library, the team's
later word, named its numeral types \TYP{IntLiteral} and \TYP{FloatLiteral},
types of values at run time without static parameters, and kept a numeral's own
type at every place that fixes no type.
The revival takes the Working Draft's names, its static parameters and the
default as its own finishing of the text; no source of the team calls those
names either final or temporary.
A \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value has one type, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, as the
revival decided on 28~September 2026 for the ranges (\secref{revival-inference}),
not \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} as \secref{natparams} says; the four numbers of a numeral
type, naturals of any size, are read in a coercion's body as values of type
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, the bound of a size to 32 bits being this implementation's,
for the lengths of arrays.
A numeral at a type of a program's own that declares no coercion from the
numeral's type is refused, since coercion does not chain; the alternative not
taken converts it into its default first and then by the type's own coercion
from that default.
A reversal to the Working Draft's polymorphic numerals would keep a numeral's
own type wherever nothing fixes a type, as the team's compiled path's own library
did, so that \EXP{x = 3} binds a numeral and \EXP{\TYP{Cell}(3)} is a
\EXP{\TYP{Cell}\llbracket\TYP{NaturalNumeral}\llbracket{}1,10,3\rrbracket\rrbracket};
a reversal to that library's numeral types would give a numeral a value when the
program runs, an \TYP{IntLiteral} or a \TYP{FloatLiteral}, to which a coercion is
applied at run time without the four numbers.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-09-numerals/design-snapshot.md},
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/plan-30/probes/draft-numerals.md},
\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md} and
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-static-numerals-spec/REPORT.md} in
the revival's repository.

\item[Effect] Both implementations convert a numeral where its place fixes a
type and give it its default elsewhere.
So \EXP{x = 3} binds a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and \EXP{x \sequiv z} is \VAR{true}
for \EXP{z\COLON\mathbb{Z}32 = 3} on both, where the compiled path answered
\VAR{false}; \EXP{y\COLON\mathbb{R}64 = 0.5} is strictly equivalent to
\EXP{a + a} for \EXP{a\COLON\mathbb{R}64 = 0.25}, \EXP{q\COLON\mathbb{Q} = 0.5}
binds \EXP{1/2}, and
\EXP{1/2 = 0.5} is \VAR{true}, where the interpreter answered otherwise
(rows~943 and~944 of the revival's gap ledger); a variable of type
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} or \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} takes a numeral, and one of type
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32} takes a numeral with one rounding, where the interpreter
refused them (row~454); a variable bound from \EXP{3000000000} is a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and reaches a declaration over \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, where the
compiled path stopped at run time (row~946); \EXP{7} passed to a parameter of
type \TYP{Object} is a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} there (row~79); a numeral outside its
type's range is a static error, where the compiled path raised an exception at
run time (row~325); a numeral at a declared floating-point type is rounded once,
where the compiled code rounded it two or three times (row~862); and a
\KWD{nat} parameter used as a value is a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, which a variable of
type \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} refuses, where the compiled type checker took it
(row~486).
\EXP{\VAR{round}(2.50000000000000001)} is 2, its numeral read as an
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64}.
A numeral that took its default prints as a value of its default type, so that
\EXP{\hbox{\rm``''}\;2.50} is \hbox{\rm``\STR{2.5}''}, and the team's test
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/NumberPrintTest.fss}, which asserted that a
numeral prints as written, is changed.
No value of a numeral type exists on either implementation when a program runs.
The compiled path, which until it is built on \library\ compiles against a
smaller library of its own, declares there the same numeral types, with
coercions generic over the four numbers from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} at its five
integer types and from \TYP{RadixPointNumeral} at \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32}; that library has no \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}.
The compiled code converts a numeral as written at a number type by that type's
coercion, whose body the compiler evaluates at the numeral's four numbers with
no knowledge of the type, into the constant that the class file holds; a value
of another representation, as one of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, and a value of a type of
a program's own come from one compiled method for each coercion from a numeral
type, which takes the four numbers as values of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and which
each place calls once, in the initialization of the class of the component that
holds the place, before the program runs, the type's prefix \EXP{-} on a
negated numeral with it; so a coercion that throws an exception stops the
program.
A signed constant at a number type of \library\ is converted from its exact
value on both implementations, outside the coercion, so that no coercion from a
numeral type receives a sign.
The interpreter, which has no static types, applies a coercion from a numeral
type at the place's first evaluation, with the four numbers bound as values of
type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, and keeps its result for the place; it refuses a numeral
only when the place is evaluated: one outside an integer type's range, one at a
type that declares no coercion from the numeral's type or whose coercion's
\KWD{where} clause the numeral does not meet, a negated numeral at a type
without a prefix \EXP{-}, a folded constant at a type of a program's own
without a coercion from the constant's default type, and a numeral bound to a
variable declared of a numeral type.
It converts a numeral that rounds to an infinity of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} or
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32} into that infinity with no error (row~967); it converts a
numeral at a parameter of the declaration that a call chooses, at a variable or
a field of a declared type and at a declared return type, but not one passed
through a tuple or a varargs parameter (rows~395 and~511).
The compiled type checker does not apply the rule that a numeral type is written
only as a parameter type to the libraries' own files.
A numeral type declares no \EXP{=} with a number type, so a numeral compared by
\EXP{=} with a number of a type other than its default meets the top-level
\EXP{=} of \library, whose parameters are of type \TYP{Any} and which takes the
numeral at its default: the interpreter answers \EXP{u = 0} \VAR{false}, and
\EXP{u \neq 0} \VAR{true}, for a zero \VAR{u} of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, none of which declares \EXP{=} with
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} (rows~966 and~NEW-A-1 of the revival's gap ledger; the
expected failure \nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/XXXNumeralEqualsNumberWalk.fss}
asserts \VAR{true}), and whether \EXP{u = 0} is \VAR{true} is open; the compiled
path's own library declares no \EXP{=} over \TYP{Any}, and declares \EXP{=} and
\EXP{\neq} on each integer type with an operand of that type, into which the
numeral is converted, so that there \EXP{u = 0} is \VAR{true} and
\EXP{u \neq 0} \VAR{false} for a zero \VAR{u} of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}.
The implementations depart from the text in these further ways, each with its
row of the revival's gap ledger: the interpreter runs the operator of
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} where a floating-point numeral stands to the left of an
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32} (row~958); a numeral with a radix point keeps only one of
its leading zeros in its digit count, as the parser gives the numeral to both
implementations (row~960); the compiled path keeps a numeral's own type,
\EXP{\TYP{NaturalNumeral}\llbracket{}n,r,v\rrbracket}, at the selector of a
\KWD{typecase} (row~963); at a place whose type names a type parameter of its
generic declaration, as \EXP{m()\COLON\TYP{Gen}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket = 3} in
\EXP{\KWD{object}\;\TYP{Box}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}, the compiled code applies
the coercion at each evaluation of the place (row~957); a coercion from a
numeral type whose body spawns a task, as an operator applied to two calls may,
stops the load of the class that holds the place, which the compiled program
loads before it starts its tasks (row~971); where a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int}
parameter of $2^{31}$ or more is used as a value, the compiled path stops with
an error that no \KWD{catch} sees, and the interpreter makes it a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} (row~962); and both leave an expression of numerals alone
as written where the form of its result needs a prefix \EXP{-} or a \EXP{/}
that its component writes nowhere (row~956).
No line of the revival's model program changes, and by reading none of its
numerals changes its value.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex},
lines 83--86, 104--108, 110--115, 117--125 and 127--129, which the numeral types
change in form; the draft notes of lines 87--102 stand:

(* The library's =/= between a number and a numeral answers NOT of their =. *)
component XXXNotEqualNumeral
export Executable

run(): () = do
    w: ZZ32 = 0
    u: NN32 = w.asNN32
    v: NN64 = w.asNN64
    d: RR64 = 0.0
    r: RR32 = narrow(d)
    q: QQ = 1/2
    assert(NOT (u =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero NN32 = 0")
    assert(NOT (v =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero NN64 = 0")
    assert(NOT (r =/= 0), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": a zero RR32 = 0")
    assert(NOT (q =/= 0.5), "opr-overview.tex, the sentence on e =/= e' that closes subsection \"GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators\": e =/= e' is NOT (e = e'), and numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\": the QQ 1/2 = 0.5")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

content.content:
## 1. Where the snapshot and the record differ

The probe followed the snapshot in each case.

- P-173 says a place fixes a type when its declared type "is a numeral type". The snapshot's point 1 and section 4 give a numeral type no value at run time, and P-174 says a numeral type is written only as a coercion's or an operator's parameter type. Built: a binding at a numeral type is refused on both paths (`tests/NumeralTypeNoValueWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/LiteralTypeUnwritable.fss`).
- A static expression at a program's own type: the snapshot's section 11 says in one bullet "only through a coercion from `ZZ32` or `QQ`" and in its last bullet "through a coercion from `QQ` or `ZZ`"; P-174 says "through its coercion from the folded value's type, such as `QQ` for `1/2`". Built: through the coercion from the folded value's default type, `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, `QQ` for a quotient, `RR64` with a radix point.
- Row 486, which the brief and the snapshot's section 11 name as standing in walk's way, is `FIXED` (`53a6074ed`) and is about the compiled checker. Walk reads a `nat` used as a value already, as a `ZZ32`, or a `ZZ64` from 2^31 (F-140). What stood in walk's way was elsewhere (section 6).
- The snapshot's section 2 quotes the Draft's `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]` with three static parameters and `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]` with four; P-174 gives the four numbers to both. Built: the Draft's arities, `NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]` and `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]`; a coercion from a natural numeral reads `m` as 0 by not having it.

## 10. What was not built

- A coercion declared in another component than the numeral's site, on the compiled path: the code generator inlines only a coercion it finds in the component it compiles (`numeralCoercionDecl`). Elsewhere the call stays at its site and the class loader instantiates the generic coercion, one class per numeral, with `v` among the stamped sizes, which `RTTIsize.of` holds as an `int`. Neither the one-method form nor a wider `RTTIsize` was built; no test reaches it.
- A site whose type names a type variable, as `m(): Gen[\T\] = 3` in `object Box[\T\]` (row 957's second case): not hoisted, as before.
- The type's `-` on a negative constant at a program's type runs at each evaluation on the compiled path; only the coercion is hoisted, where P-176 has the `-` run in the `static final` too. Under walk the whole constant is made once for the place.
- Under walk, `u = 0` for `u: NN32` and its kin give `false` (section 13, question 1). The compiled path gives `true` only because the prelude declares no `=` over `Any`.
- Under walk, a `where` clause refuses only when the place runs (P-176 until P-12), and a numeral type written as a variable's type is refused only when its binding runs.
- A numeral in a `case` expression's winning clause, an `if` without `else` or a `try` with a `finally` clause is converted by the old path, not in place; no test reached it.
- Only `where` comparisons of sizes are read; `where { v < 256 }`-style arithmetic is read with `+`, `-`, `^` and multiplication only.
- The specification is not revised: `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex` still states the field numerals (F-345), and Appendix I has no entry for the static numerals.
- Rows the prototype repairs but cannot close, since it lands nothing: 318, 362, 957 (first case), 961, 968, 969, 970, and row 513 for a numeral coercion.

## 11. Findings the record does not hold

- Row 971 (filed): on the compiled path a numeral site's coercion that spawns a task fails the load of the component's class, since the static initializer runs before the task pool; batch 29's sites fail so on the base (the probe in section 5).
- Row 972 (filed): a library component with a generic overloaded top-level function stores its inference cache tables into a class named without its package, and every compiled program dies at its static initializer. No library component has one today.
- Row 291's crash, `BoxedUnit cannot be cast` in the post-check walker, has a second trigger: a size inference variable left in a checked library (section 3). Not filed: the row's notes have 29 characters left; the trigger needs the probe's library to show.
- Walk's sizes are `long` (`IntNat.java`), and walk refuses a size above `NN32` when it binds one (`EvalType.java:252-262`); the record holds the second (F-140), not the first as the limit of a numeral's `v`.
- The checker coerces an `if`'s non-winning clauses, and a tuple of numerals at a tuple type, as whole expressions (`impls/Misc.scala:556-564`, `CoercionOracle.checkCoercionTuple`), so with batch 29's `IntLiteral` a numeral there was coerced at run time. Not a defect today; it matters only once numerals have no run-time value.
- The prelude's own code writes getters on numerals, `(1).asZZ` and `(1).asNN32` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:561-570`, `:750`, `:752`, `:814`, `:816`).

## 12. Decisions

1. The hierarchy, where the Draft is silent ("We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy", `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:93-95`, kept in the revived `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:123-126`): `Numeral` below `Number`, the record's "a sibling of the number types under `Number`" (`references/revival-changes.md`, "Numbers"); `NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]` and `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]` at the Draft's arities, below two `Any` traits that exclude each other. Not taken: the Draft's `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix` and `RadixPointNumeralWithExplicitRadix` (the radix is `r`, as P-174 has it), its `Literal[\v\]`, and a generic `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]` above both, which the exclusion rule forbids beside the two generic traits; `Numeral excludes { Number }`, which the promotion of P-74 cannot use: with it the team's `compiler_tests/InferO2Num` failed, one of the four failures of section 7's run of 45 tests. This is a decision not taken for the curator too (question 4).
2. The four numbers read as values inside a numeral coercion are `ZZ`; elsewhere a `nat` stays a `ZZ32` (P-173). The brief's "exact integers"; the alternative, every `nat` value a `ZZ`, changes P-173 and its tests.
3. At a built-in target the compiled fold is batch 29's, recognised by the target type; the checker reaches it through the library's generic coercion. The alternative, evaluating the library coercion's body at compile time, needs an evaluator in the compiler. Under walk the library's coercion body runs, as for any type.
4. On the compiled path the coercion is inlined at its site, not compiled as one method that takes the four numbers as values (section 5 gives why).
5. The fold marks its results by their text, `-3` and `(5)`, so that the checker, the code generator and walk tell a numeral as written from a negated one and from a folded static expression. The alternative, a field on the node, changes `Fortress.ast`.
6. At the library's eight types the range refusal stays batch 29's, by the value, not a `where` clause on each library coercion: `-2147483648` at `ZZ32` is a negative constant, which a `where` over `v` cannot see.
7. Under walk the parameter of a numeral coercion is bound to `()`, and the conversion runs when dispatch first asks whether a declaration admits the numeral.
8. The prelude keeps no `IntLiteral`; a size read as a value reaches the code as a `ZZ32`, with row 962's error kept.
9. The eight walk assertions of `u = 0` and its kin move to an `XXX` test that asserts the snapshot's answer, since the snapshot's section 11 states it; the compiled path's test keeps `u = 0`.

## 13. Questions for the curator, as decisions not taken

1. `u = 0` for `u: NN32`, under walk, and on the compiled path after the switch-over.
   - The question: with the `=` pairs over the numeral types deleted, `u = 0` meets two declarations: the library's `=` over `Any`, which the numeral's default `ZZ32` fits as it is, and `NN32`'s own `=`, which the numeral reaches by its conversion. Which runs?
   - Sources: the snapshot's section 11 (confirmed 11-09, 15:xx to 16:3x UTC): "the checker fixes `0` at `NN32` from the other operand and folds it"; the tree's rule "A conversion never changes which declaration runs when one already fits" (`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/SKILL.md`, "Fortress as a language"), which walk applies (`OverloadedFunction.bestMatchForNumeralsInternal`); P-173's `gg(5, w)` (P-49).
   - Solutions: (a) a numeral reaches a declaration by its conversion before one it fits only at its default, where that declaration is more specific; this changes the tree's rule, and walk's dispatch; (b) `u = 0` is `false`, strict equivalence of an `NN32` and a `ZZ32`; (c) the `=` pairs stay, against "It was a wrong choice and it gets deleted".
   - Current behaviour: in the tree today the `=` pairs give `true`; with the prototype walk gives `false` and the compiled path `true`, since the prelude has no `=` over `Any`. Built: the compiled answer; walk's is the `XXX` test.
2. The library's own types and "a separate way in the compiler for the shipped numerics".
   - The question: the library's eight types take a numeral by the same generic coercion, and the checker finds it so; but the compiled fold to a JVM constant is recognised by the target type, and the range refusal is by the value, not a `where` clause. Is that the hole his words name, or the folding of a constructor call whose result is a JVM `int`?
   - Sources: the snapshot's section 11, first bullet; decisions 3 and 6.
   - Solutions: (a) keep it; (b) `where` clauses on the library coercions, with a reading of a negative constant's sign (`-2147483648` at `ZZ32` must fit); (c) a compile-time evaluator of the library coercions' bodies.
   - Current behaviour: (a), as batch 29 built it.
3. A folded static expression at a program's own type.
   - The question: through which coercion does `10/20`, or `2 + 3`, reach a program's type?
   - Sources: the snapshot's section 11, one bullet "only through a coercion from `ZZ32` or `QQ`" and its last "through a coercion from `QQ` or `ZZ`" (both 11-09, 15:xx to 16:3x UTC); P-174, "through its coercion from the folded value's type, such as `QQ` for `1/2`" (section 1).
   - Solutions: (a) from the folded value's default type, `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, `QQ` for a quotient, `RR64` with a radix point; (b) from `ZZ` for an integer, whatever its value, and `QQ` for the rest; (c) from `ZZ32` or `QQ` only.
   - Current behaviour: in the tree today the fold writes a constant as a numeral (`IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.written`), so it reaches a program's type through the type's coercion from the numeral type, as a numeral does; built: (a).
4. The numeral type hierarchy.
   - The question: which traits are the numeral types, and may a program extend them?
   - Sources: the Draft's note "We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:93-95`, 2009); its `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix` and `Literal[\v\]` (`:83-129`); P-174, the four numbers.
   - Solutions: (a) the probe's five traits (decision 1); (b) the Draft's six types, which the rule that no type extends two instantiations of one generic trait refuses for `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]` above both kinds; (c) (a) with `comprises` clauses, so that no program extends them, not tried.
   - Current behaviour: the tree's field numerals have three traits without static parameters; built: (a).
5. A coercion that spawns, at a place on the compiled path (row 971).
   - The question: where does a site's coercion run, given that a component's static initializer runs before the task pool?
   - Sources: P-176, "into a `static final` field filled when the class loads"; `MainWrapper.java:61-63`.
   - Solutions: (a) start the task pool before the program's classes load; (b) fill each site at its first use, on the task that reaches it, which changes P-176's "filled when the class loads"; (c) run the static initializer's coercions on the pool.
   - Current behaviour: the class's load fails, on the base and with the prototype; nothing was changed.
6. A coercion declared in another component than the numeral's site, on the compiled path.
   - The question: how does the compiled path apply a generic coercion whose body it cannot inline?
   - Sources: P-176; the snapshot's section 9, question 3, "What does `v` of a 20-digit numeral need in the checker, and in the class loader's stamped constants (F-129)?"; `RTTIsize.of`, which holds a size as an `int` (section 10).
   - Solutions: (a) one method per coercion that takes the four numbers as `ZZ` values, called once per place; (b) the class loader's instantiation, one class per numeral, with `RTTIsize` widened to a `BigInteger`; (c) inlining across components from the analyzed cache.
   - Current behaviour: the call stays at its site and is instantiated by the class loader; no test reaches it.

## 14. Where the Draft is silent, and what was chosen

- The hierarchy (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:123-126`, the team's note): decision 1.
- When a coercion runs: the Draft says nothing (the snapshot's section 2); P-176: once per place, at load on the compiled path, at the first evaluation under walk.
- The four numbers of a numeral with trailing zeros: as written, `3.14150` is 314150 and 5, batch 29's reading kept (`NumeralNumbers.of`).
- A radix indicator: the Draft's `...WithExplicitRadix` types are not built; `r` carries the radix, as P-174 has it.
- The sign: the Draft's natural numeral has no sign; the curator's 23:10 on 11-08 and repair 3 give the rest (P-174).

## 15. Commands worked out

\end{quote}
The other passages this change revises are the revival's own text, not the
Working Draft's.
\nolinkurl{Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines 149--165, said,
before this revision:
\begin{quote}
In \library, every numeral without a radix point has the type
\TYP{IntLiteral}, which extends \TYP{Number} and none of the number types
(\secref{basic-rationals}); each of the five integer types
(\secref{basic-integers}), \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} declares a
coercion from it.
\end{quote}
and its box said that ``the compiled type checker gives every numeral without a
radix point that type'', and that the interpreter ``gives such a numeral the
type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} when its
value does not fit in the narrower type, and it is to give it the type
\TYP{IntLiteral} once it runs with the static types of the compiled type
checker''.
The box of \secref{coercion} said, in
\nolinkurl{Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex}, lines 84--88:
\begin{quote}
\Library\ give an integer numeral the type \TYP{IntLiteral}, from which
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} coerces, and the compiled type checker types a numeral so
(\secref{literals}, \secref{revival-numeral-type}).
The interpreter does not yet: it gives an integer numeral outside the range of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} a wider integer type, and so does not yet convert it.
\end{quote}
\nolinkurl{Specification/basic/inference.tex}, lines 185--187, said that
\EXP{b\COLON\mathbb{Z}64 = \VAR{id}(3)} ``instantiates \VAR{id} at the
numeral's own type (\secref{literals}) and coerces the result'', and lines
304--307 said that a numeral whose conversions tie ``is read as a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, or as a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} when its
value does not fit in the narrower type''.
\nolinkurl{Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex}, line 43, said that
``\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (\STR{RR64}) coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, from
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and from integer numerals''.
The effect of \secref{revival-numeral-type} said:
\begin{quote}
Inequality is not converted: the top-level declaration of \EXP{\neq}, whose
parameters are of type \TYP{Any}, is applicable to an integer value and a
numeral without coercion, and the compiled type checker selects it and converts
neither operand.
\end{quote}
and that ``\TYP{IntLiteral} declares its own \VAR{zero}, \VAR{one}, \VAR{even},
\VAR{odd}, \VAR{floor}, \VAR{ceiling}, \VAR{truncate}, \OPR{DIVIDES},
\OPR{TIMES} and a power with a numeral exponent'', and that ``the interpreter
still gives an integer numeral the type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}
or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} by its value, so a numeral reaches none of the declarations
of \TYP{IntLiteral} there''.
The rationale of \secref{revival-inference} said that ``the compiled type
checker gives a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter used as a value the type of a
numeral'', and its effect that ``where the conversions of a numeral tie, the
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} declaration or instance is taken''.
The rationale of \secref{revival-asfloat} named ``the numeral type
\TYP{IntLiteral}'' among the types that declare \VAR{asFloat}, and its effect
named ``the library's 21 coercions between number types''.
The effect of \secref{revival-object-kinds} said that \library\ declare ``the
two numeral objects of the interpreter'' as value objects, and named two
departures:
\begin{quote}
the interpreter gives a floating-point numeral bound to a variable of type
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} the type of the numeral object, so it is not strictly
equivalent to a computed \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} value of the same bits;
an integer numeral is a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} value in the interpreter, by its magnitude, and a numeral
object to the compiled type checker, so a numeral
compared with a typed value can answer differently on the two paths;
\end{quote}
\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/types-vals-vars.tex}, lines 494--500,
which the numeral types change in form:
\begin{quote}
\Library\ define simple standard types for literals such as
\EXP{\TYP{BooleanLiteral}\llbracket{}b\rrbracket},
\TYP{()} (pronounced ``void''),
\TYP{Character}, \TYP{String}, and
\EXP{\TYP{Numeral}\llbracket{}n,m,r,v\rrbracket}
for appropriate values of \VAR{b}, \VAR{n}, \VAR{m}, \VAR{r}, and \VAR{v}
(See \secref{literals} for a discussion of Fortress literals).
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C: the numeral types lie below
\TYP{Numeral}, beside the number types under \TYP{Number}, and no number type
is a subtype of a numeral type or a numeral type of a number type, whichever
rule on instantiations the compiled type checker keeps.
\end{description}

the results of dividing any integer by any nonzero integer,
and three more elements:
\EXP{+\infty} and \EXP{-\infty} (written \EXP{1/0} and \EXP{-1/0}),
the results of dividing a positive or a negative integer by zero,
and the indefinite rational (written \EXP{0/0}), which is used as the result
of dividing zero by zero or of adding \EXP{-\infty} to \EXP{+\infty}.

The number types of this chapter are
the integer types \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} (\secref{basic-integers}),
the rational type \EXP{\mathbb{Q}},
and the floating-point types \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (\STR{RR64}) and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} (\STR{RR32}).
They are siblings under the trait \TYP{Number}:
each is a subtype of \TYP{Number}, and none is a subtype of another.
Some conversions between them are coercions (\chapref{conversions-coercions}),
each declared by the type converted to;
since coercions do not chain (\secref{coercion}), each pair is declared.
Those among the integer types are given in \secref{basic-integers};
the others are these:

\begin{tabbing}
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}} (\STR{QQ}) coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, and from both numeral types (\secref{literals}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} (\STR{RR64}) coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and from both numeral types.
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32} (\STR{RR32}) coerces from both numeral types.
\end{tabbing}
Each of the five integer types coerces from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} too.
A coercion from a numeral type is generic over the numeral's four numbers, the
static arguments of its type, as
\EXP{\KWD{coerce}\llbracket\KWD{nat} n,\KWD{nat} r,\KWD{nat} v\rrbracket(x\COLON \TYP{NaturalNumeral}\llbracket{}n,r,v\rrbracket)},
and computes the type's value from them (\secref{literals}): exactly into the
integer types and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, and with one rounding, to the nearest value
of the type, into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}.
Since no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, a numeral type
declares no \EXP{=} with a number type, and no number type declares one with a
numeral type.

Every other conversion between number types is written explicitly;
in particular, a conversion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} from
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, or \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}
is explicit, written \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)} with the method that each of these types declares;
\TYP{Number} itself declares no conversion, and the numeral types declare no
\VAR{asFloat}.

numerals among the sources of the coercion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} only.

converts from \TYP{NaturalNumeral}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and

convert into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}.}

as the one floating-point type, and \library\ declared \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} a
subtype of it, so that a value of \EXP{\mathbb{R}32} was also a value of

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### Numbers

POSITIONS.md:99
- P-165 **`asFloat` and the `=` built on it leave `trait Number`; each built-in number type keeps its own `asFloat`.** `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64` each declare `asFloat`, so the written conversion `asFloat(x)` into `RR64` is unchanged at every concrete type; the numeral types declare none, since no numeral value exists when a program runs (P-174). Two numbers of different types compare by `=` only where a coercion carries one into the other (P-74); otherwise the program writes the conversion, `asFloat(x) = y`. The vector norm takes a bound that promises a float; its form is the default of a fork on his review list: the norm at each of the eight number types, each by its own `asFloat` (F-324). `Float`'s `^` at a `Number` exponent, `random`, `atan2` and `printThreadInfo` are declared at `RR64`, and coercion carries `ZZ32`, `RR32` and numerals to them. The specification's sentence follows (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:56-73`). P-74's rule, an exact conversion implicit and a lossy one written, stands. Why: the team's compiler prelude declares `Number` with nothing in it (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:510`), and the specification does not ground the method: its sentence that names it on `Number` is the revival's revision. The curator's rule for such a case: an early idea of the interpreter's library goes where the specification does not ground it and the later prelude eliminated it. With `Number` open (P-160), an abstract `asFloat` would force a program's own number, such as a complex number, to invent a float, and `Number`'s `=` would compare two different complex numbers by it.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The one library and the compiled checker

POSITIONS.md:35
- P-37 **One library, the interpreter's, is the library that the compiler checks.** The interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`, becomes the compiled path's prelude in place of the compiler's own, and the compiled path reads the interpreter's library with it. Why: the switch-over spares porting the interpreter's library into the compiler's; the revival develops the checker until it accepts that fuller library. The curator sees the compiler's prelude, its own library files `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin` and `CompilerAlgebra`, as a bootstrap to remove. So no declaration is added to the compiler's prelude, and at the switch-over its three files are deleted and their tests kept (P-38 says which tests are respelled; F-293 holds the compiler's fourth file, `CompilerSystem`). The one exception is the numerals: until the switch-over the prelude carries the design of P-174 and P-176, so that both paths treat a numeral alike before it, and that copy goes with the prelude. The decision settles which files survive, not the designs inside them: the one library takes a design of the prelude's where it is the team's later decision, as it took the prelude's flat shape of the number types. This decision does not stop work on the code generator, which is compiler work under either library.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The standard and the sources

POSITIONS.md:24
- P-26 **The team's later decision wins over its earlier one, in a text or in code, where the team made it the language's rule.** P-7 names the texts, from the Working Draft to the POPL 2019 paper. Code counts as a decision where the team built it alike for all its types, or stated its rule in a commit message, a comment or the checker. Code that its author called a stub, and code that works around a limit of the JVM or of the checker, serve only the implementation. The decision that they depart from stands. "Later" is the date of the team's work on the point at issue. The revival revises `Specification/` to follow a later decision. The one library follows it too, in place of the team's earlier code, such as the interpreter's library. Where two later decisions conflict, the goal decides (P-8). The implementers' later word also outweighs unfinished text. Why: the Working Draft's early text was a wish. The type group, the part of the team that built the type checker and the compiler, then worked to make the language run. So they learned what is feasible. They sought performance, and specialization was a must. Their later decisions include the exclusion rule, specialization and the number types of the compiler's prelude, siblings from 2009 to 2012 (P-43). The revival knows less than they did, so it does not second-guess them.
